enabled.name: Connection · Bridge on
enabled.hint: Connects this world to the MCP server on the Gamemaster's PC. Only a Gamemaster's browser connects.

connectionType.name: Connection · Connection type
connectionType.hint: This module always connects over WebSocket, on HTTPS pages as well. The WebRTC choice is kept for worlds that stored it and connects over WebSocket too.

serverHost.name: Connection · Server address
serverHost.hint: Where the MCP server runs. localhost when it runs on the same PC as this browser.

serverPort.name: Connection · Server port
serverPort.hint: Port of the bridge on the PC.

allowWriteOperations.name: Writing · Allow Write Operations
allowWriteOperations.hint: The switch before everything else. Off means the AI changes nothing in this world, whatever the levels below say. Tools of other modules are held by it too, unless they only read.

permScenes.name: Permissions · Scenes
permScenes.hint: What the AI may do with scenes. Deleting is off by default, because it cannot be undone.

permPlaylists.name: Permissions · Playlists
permPlaylists.hint: What the AI may do with playlists. Deleting is off by default, because it cannot be undone.

permJournals.name: Permissions · Journals
permJournals.hint: What the AI may do with journals. Deleting is off by default, because it cannot be undone.

permRollTables.name: Permissions · Roll tables
permRollTables.hint: What the AI may do with roll tables. Deleting is off by default, because it cannot be undone.

permActors.name: Permissions · Actors
permActors.hint: What the AI may do with actors. Deleting is off by default, because it cannot be undone.

permFolders.name: Permissions · Folders
permFolders.hint: What the AI may do with folders. Deleting is off by default, because it cannot be undone.

permCompendiums.name: Permissions · Compendiums
permCompendiums.hint: What the AI may do with compendiums. Deleting is off by default, because it cannot be undone.

toolProviderModules.name: Permissions · Modules with their own tools
toolProviderModules.hint: Ids of modules that may offer the AI tools of their own, separated by commas, for example ninjos-shops. None by default: a tool of another module runs its own code and works around the levels above.

werkzeugModule.name: Modules with their own tools (old key)

enableNotifications.name: Behaviour · Connection messages
enableNotifications.hint: Shows a message when the bridge connects, disconnects, or stays down for a minute.

autoReconnectEnabled.name: Behaviour · Reconnect automatically
autoReconnectEnabled.hint: Tries again after a lost connection: quickly at first, then every 30 seconds, without giving up.

heartbeatInterval.name: Behaviour · Heartbeat in seconds
heartbeatInterval.hint: How often the module checks that the connection is really alive. A dead connection is closed and then reconnected.

indicator.unknownDetail: The module is loaded but reports no state.
indicator.offDetail: The bridge is switched off in the module settings.
indicator.blockedDetail: The MCP server on the PC does not accept connections from {origin}. Add the address to FOUNDRY_ALLOWED_ORIGINS there, or delete allowed-origins.json so it learns this address again.
indicator.standbyDetail: Another tab or world holds the bridge ({world}). This tab takes over when that one closes.
indicator.downDetail: No bridge to {where}. Is the MCP server running on the PC? The bridge reconnects on its own once it is. Click to try right away.

notify.disconnected: MCP bridge disconnected. It reconnects on its own.
notify.serverUnreachable: The MCP server on the PC is not reachable at {url}. Start it there; the bridge connects on its own as soon as it runs.
notify.lostConnection: The MCP bridge has been down for a minute. It keeps trying every 30 seconds.
notify.rejected: The MCP server on the PC refused this page: {reason}
